items.rationale: Memory between sessions is storage outside the model: the program saved the fact and put it into the new session's context. No weights change and the model keeps no per-user state. Choosing a or d shows the belief that the model itself learned or stored the fact.

Call 1 input is 1,050. Call 2 is 1,050 + 50 + 400 = 1,500. Call 3 is 1,500 + 50 + 1,000 = 2,550. The total is 5,100, because each call re-sends the whole transcript. An answer of 2,550 counts only the last call; 1,550 or 2,500 counts each item once.

Context rot: recall and accuracy can degrade as the token count grows, even when everything fits in the window. The other options invent behaviours: nothing is ignored after the third chunk and the window is not reset.

items.answer: The application (the program around the model) writes it to storage it controls, and the model gets the result back as a tool result.
accepted: The program writes it and returns the result to the model
Your application runs the request and sends back a tool result
The client code does the write and the model receives a tool_result
The app writes the note and the model gets the outcome as a tool result
items.rationale: Client-side means the model only requests the operation; the application executes it against its own storage and returns the outcome in a tool result, as with any other tool. An answer that says the model writes to disk itself has the same mistake as the model running its own tools.

Just-in-time search lets the model look again with a better query, at the cost of extra model calls, tokens and time. Search never changes training data, and chunking is still needed so each result is small.
